explanation.en: City of David and setting of Ruth, Micah prophesied that out of me would come forth the Ruler of Israel, born in the flesh.
explanation.am: የዳዊት ከተማ ነኝ፤ ሚክያስ አለቃ እንደሚወጣብኝ ተነበየ፤ መድኃኒታችን ኢየሱስ ክርስቶስ በሥጋ የተወለደብኝ ቅድስት ስፍራ ነኝ።

explanation.en: I confronted the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel, prayed for fire from heaven, and was taken up in a chariot of fire.
explanation.am: በቀርሜሎስ ተራራ የሐሰት ነቢያትን ተጋፈጥሁ፤ እሳት ከሰማይ በጸሎት አወረድሁ፤ በእሳት ሰረገላም ወደ ሰማይ ዐረግሁ።

explanation.en: I took up the mantle of Elijah, asked for a double portion of his spirit, and healed Naaman of leprosy in the Jordan.
explanation.am: የኤልያስን ካባ ወረስሁ፤ የመንፈሱን ሁለት ዕጥፍ ተቀበልሁ፤ ሶርያዊውን ንዕማንን በዮርዳኖስ ውኃ ፈወስሁ።

explanation.en: Raised by Mordecai in Shushan, I fasted for three days and risked my life before King Ahasuerus to save my people.
explanation.am: በሱሳ በመርዶክዮስ እጅ አደግሁ፤ ለሦስት ቀን ጾም አወጅሁ፤ “ከጠፋሁም ልጥፋ” ብዬ ሕዝቤን ከመጥፋት አዳንሁ።

explanation.en: Encompassed by mountains, home to Mount Zion and the holy Temple, where Christ entered with palms and achieved our redemption.
explanation.am: በተራሮች የተከበብሁ የሰላም ከተማ ነኝ፤ ሰሎሞን መቅደሱን ሠራብኝ፤ ጌታችን በሆሣዕና ገብቶ በጎልጎታ የመስቀል ድነት ፈጸመብኝ።

explanation.en: I wore camel’s hair, cried in the wilderness to prepare the way of the Lord, and baptized Christ in the Jordan.
explanation.am: የግመል ጠጕር ለበስሁ፤ በምድረ በዳ የጌታን መንገድ ጠረግሁ፤ ጌታችን ኢየሱስ ክርስቶስን በዮርዳኖስ አጠመቅሁ።

explanation.en: Sold by my brothers into Egypt, I interpreted Pharaoh’s dreams of seven kine and preserved life during the famine.
explanation.am: በወንድሞቼ ወደ ግብፅ ተሸጥሁ፤ የፈርዖንን ሕልም ፈታሁ፤ በራብ ዘመን ቤተሰቦቼንና ዓለምን በምግብ አዳንሁ።

explanation.en: I succeeded Moses, led the twelve tribes across the Jordan behind the Ark of the Covenant, and took Jericho.
explanation.am: ሙሴን ተክቼ ሕዝቡን መራሁ፤ በቃል ኪዳኑ ታቦት ፊት ዮርዳኖስን አሻገርሁ፤ የኢያሪኮንም ቅጥር አፈረስሁ።

explanation.en: I trembled with smoke and lightning as God descended, Moses spoke face-to-face, and the stone tablets of the Law were given.
explanation.am: እግዚአብሔር በእሳት ሲወርድ በጭስና በመብረቅ ተናወጥሁ፤ ሙሴ አርባ ቀን ቆየብኝ፤ አሥርቱ ትእዛዛት የተጻፉባቸው ጽላቶች ተሰጡብኝ።

explanation.en: I was the older brother of Moses who served as his spokesman and became the first High Priest of Israel.
I was a woman of good understanding and beauty who intervened with gifts to prevent David from shedding blood over Nabal’s folly.
I was a disciple of John the Baptist who first found my brother Simon Peter and brought him to Jesus.
I was an eighty-four-year-old widow who departed not from the Temple with fastings and gave thanks when the Christ child arrived.
My name means Son of Encouragement; I sold a field to lay the money at the apostles’ feet and vouched for Saul in Jerusalem.
I was a wealthy and righteous man of Bethlehem who showed kindness to Ruth in my barley fields and redeemed her as my wife.
I was the bronze-covered wooden altar set before the door of the Tabernacle where morning and evening sacrifices were offered.
I was one of the two faithful spies who believed God would give Israel the promised land, and I inherited Hebron in my old age.
I was a devout Roman centurion in Caesarea who gave alms and prayed continually, to whom Peter was sent to preach the Gospel.
I was a prophetess and judge in Israel who held court under a palm tree and inspired Barak to victory over Sisera.
I was the wife of Zechariah the priest who, filled with the Holy Spirit, welcomed the Virgin Mary as the mother of my Lord.
I was a priest and skilled scribe who led exiles back from Babylon and taught the statutes and laws of God to the community.
God tested my faith with the morning dew on a fleece, and I defeated the Midianite multitude with only three hundred men.
I hold fragrant incense before the presence of the Lord, symbolizing the acceptable prayers of all the saints ascending to heaven.
I prayed with tears in the tabernacle at Shiloh for a son, and after God gave me Samuel, I dedicated him to divine service.
I trusted in the Lord, reopened the Temple, held a great Passover, and God added fifteen years to my life after I prayed.
God instructed me to marry an unfaithful wife as a living sign of His enduring, merciful love for wayward Israel.
I was the child of promise born to Abraham and Sarah in their old age, and I carried the wood for the sacrifice on Mount Moriah.
I wrestled with an angel until dawn at Peniel, received the name Israel, and fathered the twelve tribes.
I was John’s brother, one of the three who witnessed the Transfiguration, and the first of the Twelve Apostles martyred by Herod.
I remained steadfast in faith through severe trials and loss, declaring: I know that my Redeemer lives.
I was in the belly of a great fish for three days and three nights before preaching repentance to the people of Nineveh.
I was King Saul’s son who formed a covenant of deep, selfless friendship with David and protected him from my father’s wrath.
I was the waters where Joshua led the ark into the promised land, where Naaman washed seven times, and where Jesus was baptized.
I became king at eight years old, wept when the Book of the Law was discovered in the Temple, and purged the land of idolatry.
I was the elder daughter of Laban who became Jacob’s first wife and bore Judah, from whose line the Messiah came.
I was sitting at the tax collector’s booth when Jesus called me to follow Him, and I wrote the Gospel opening with His royal genealogy.
I watched over my baby brother Moses in the Nile and led the women in singing praise with timbrels after crossing the Red Sea.
I uncovered a plot against the king, refused to bow to Haman, and urged Queen Esther to advocate for our people.
I was the coastal mountain where the prophet Elijah confronted the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and fire fell from heaven.
I was the Galilean town where the Archangel Gabriel appeared to Mary and where Jesus grew up with Joseph and His Mother.
I was from Bethsaida, invited Nathanael to come and see Jesus, and asked the Lord to show us the Father at the Last Supper.
I was Jacob’s beloved wife whom he met at the well in Haran, and the mother of Joseph and Benjamin.
I was a Nazirite blessed with extraordinary strength who fought the Philistines with a donkey’s jawbone.
The Holy Spirit promised I would not see death before beholding the Lord’s Christ, whom I cradled in the Temple.
I was an almond staff that miraculously blossomed, budded, and yielded ripe almonds overnight to confirm the divine choice of the priesthood.
I was a keeper of sheep who offered to God the firstlings of my flock with sincere faith, whose righteous blood cried out from the ground.
I was the commander-in-chief of King Saul’s army who later sought to unite all Israel under King David in Hebron.
I was formed from the dust of the earth in the image and likeness of God, named the living creatures, and was placed in the Garden of Eden.
I was an eloquent Alexandrian who was fervent in spirit and mighty in the Scriptures, whom Aquila and Priscilla instructed more perfectly.
I was a Jewish tentmaker from Pontus who fled Rome with my wife Priscilla, lodged Paul in Corinth, and risked my neck for the church.
I led ten thousand men from Naphtali and Zebulun to Mount Tabor when Deborah called me, routing the army of Sisera.
I was the faithful scribe of Jeremiah who recorded his prophecies on a scroll and read them boldly in the Lord’s house.
I was an eighty-year-old elder of Rogelim who provided food and supplies for David and his men while fleeing Absalom at Mahanaim.
I was a valiant captain of David’s mighty men who struck down a lion in a pit on a snowy day and guarded the king’s throne.
I was Jacob’s youngest son born on the journey near Bethlehem, in whose grain sack the silver cup was placed in Egypt.
I was the village fifteen stadia from Jerusalem, the home of Mary, Martha, and Lazarus, where Christ was welcomed and lodged.
I was fashioned by Moses and mounted upon a pole in the wilderness so that whoever looked upon me was healed from venomous serpent bites.
I was the lakeside city in Galilee that served as the center of Jesus’ public ministry, called His own city, where He taught in the synagogue.
I resolved not to defile myself with the king’s delicacies, interpreted Nebuchadnezzar’s dreams, and survived unharmed in the den of lions.
I was a left-handed judge from the tribe of Benjamin who delivered Israel from Moabite oppression by striking King Eglon with a double-edged dagger.
I walked faithfully with God for three hundred years, and God took me so that I did not see death.
I was formed from Adam’s rib to be his helper and companion, and I was called the mother of all living.
I was King David’s seer who gave him the choice of three divine chastisements and instructed him to build an altar on Araunah’s threshing floor.
I challenged the returned exiles saying: Is it time for you to dwell in paneled houses while this house lies in ruins? Build the temple!
I was one of the three holy youths who refused to bow before the golden image in Babylon and walked freely through the blazing fiery furnace.
I stood alongside Aaron on the hill at Rephidim to support Moses’ uplifted arms until sunset so Israel could prevail.
I was one of the Twelve Apostles chosen by the Lord Jesus Christ, distinguished in the apostolic lists from the son of Zebedee.
I sent Levites throughout Judah with the Book of the Law to teach the people and appointed singers before the army singing: Praise the Lord.
I was a mighty warrior from Gilead who defeated the Ammonites after making a solemn vow to the Lord.
I was the father of eight sons in Bethlehem who sent young David with bread to his brothers, from whose root the Messiah sprouted.
I was the priest of Midian whose daughter Zipporah married Moses, and I advised Moses to appoint capable judges over Israel.
I was a honorable counselor and secret disciple who boldly asked Pilate for the body of Jesus and wrapped Him in linen in my own tomb.
I was a righteous craftsman from Nazareth whom an angel warned in dreams to take Mary and the Child into Egypt to escape Herod.
I was the post-exilic High Priest who stood before the Angel of the Lord while Satan accused me, and my filthy garments were replaced with rich robes.
I offered myself as surety for Benjamin before Joseph in Egypt, and my father prophesied that the scepter would not depart from my line.
I was a devout widow who fasted on my roof in Bethulia, entered the enemy camp, and delivered Israel by striking Holofernes.
I reigned in Judah with righteousness, removed pagan shrines, relied on God to defeat Zerah the Ethiopian’s army, and repaired the Lord’s altar.
I prospered greatly as king in building towers and agriculture, but became proud and attempted to burn incense in the sanctuary.
I was Jesus’ friend who lay four days in the tomb until He stood outside and called out with a loud voice: Come forth!
I was a seller of purple cloth in Philippi whose heart the Lord opened to heed Paul’s words, and the first European convert baptized with my household.
I was Samson’s father from the tribe of Dan who offered a young goat upon a rock while the Angel of the Lord ascended in the flame.
I was serving diligently in my house when Jesus visited and confessed: Yes, Lord, I believe that You are the Christ, the Son of God.
I sat at Jesus’ feet listening to His teaching and later anointed His feet with costly spikenard, wiping them with my hair.
I accompanied the Lord from John’s baptism to the Ascension, and was chosen by prayer and lot in the upper room to fill the twelfth apostolic seat.
I was the King of Salem and priest of the Most High God who brought forth bread and wine and blessed Abraham.
I was Jonathan’s son, lame in both feet, whom David welcomed to eat continually at the royal table for the sake of his father.
I was the mountain range upon which Noah’s ark came to rest on the seventeenth day of the seventh month as the floodwaters receded.
I was the mountain of God where Moses saw the burning bush unconsumed and where Elijah heard the still, small voice in the cave.
I was the mountain where Abraham bound Isaac for sacrifice and where King Solomon later constructed the glorious Temple of Jerusalem.
I was the eastern ridge overlooking Jerusalem where Christ wept over the city, delivered the end-times discourse, and ascended into heaven.
I was the high mountain in Galilee where the Lord Jesus Christ was transfigured in divine glory before Peter, James, and John.
I was the Elkoshite who proclaimed comfort to Judah by foretelling the utter destruction and overthrow of Nineveh.
I returned from the land of Moab to Bethlehem in grief calling myself Mara, but rejoiced when Ruth bore Obed, David’s grandfather.
I confronted King David with the parable of the poor man’s ewe lamb, announced God’s eternal covenant, and anointed Solomon.
Jesus saw me sitting under the fig tree before Philip called me, and declared me an Israelite indeed in whom there is no deceit.
I was a ruler of the Jews who came to Jesus by night to ask about being born again, and later brought myrrh and aloes for His burial.
I wrote a single-chapter prophecy denouncing Edom’s arrogance in the rock clefts and proclaiming deliverance upon Mount Zion.
I was Caleb’s younger nephew who conquered Kiriath-sepher, received Achsah as my wife, and became the very first judge of Israel.
I was a hospitable Christian leader in Colossae whose house hosted the church, to whom Paul appealed to welcome Onesimus as a beloved brother.
I was the grandson of Aaron zealous for God’s holiness who turned away the divine plague and received a covenant of perpetual priesthood.
I was the pool with five porches by the Sheep Gate where Jesus healed a paralyzed man who had suffered for thirty-eight years.
I was the pool in Jerusalem whose name means Sent, where Jesus sent the man blind from birth to wash the clay and receive sight.
I welcomed the two spies into Jericho, hid them under stalks of flax, hung a scarlet cord in my window, and was saved with my family.
I drew water from the well for Abraham’s servant and his ten camels in Mesopotamia, and I became Isaac’s beloved wife.
I was granted to Adam and Eve in place of Abel, and in my days men began to call upon the name of the Lord.
I was the son of Anath who struck down six hundred Philistine warriors with an oxgoad to deliver Israel.
I was an acacia table overlaid with pure gold in the Holy Place, carrying twelve loaves of presentation bread continually before God.
I was a leading brother from Jerusalem who accompanied Paul on his second missionary journey, singing hymns at midnight in the Philippian jail.
I was called the Zealot or Canaanite among the Twelve, who abandoned worldly political fervor to follow Christ with fervent spiritual zeal.
I was a disciple in Joppa full of good works and almsgiving who made tunics for widows, whom the apostle Peter raised from the dead.
I kept the pledge of the signet ring and staff, gave birth to Perez and Zerah, and am named in the royal genealogy of Jesus Christ.
I declared: My Lord and my God, after seeing the wounds of the Risen Christ, and preached the Gospel unto India.
I learned the Holy Scriptures from my youth through my grandmother Lois and mother Eunice, and was appointed bishop of Ephesus by Paul.
I was Paul’s loyal true child in our common faith whom he left in Crete to set in order things that were lacking and appoint elders in every city.
I was a righteous captive in Nineveh who buried the dead and gave alms, whose blindness was healed by the gall of a fish guided by Archangel Raphael.
I was a wealthy chief tax collector of Jericho of short stature who climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus and pledged half my goods to the poor.
I was the faithful priest who remained loyal to David during Absalom’s rebellion and anointed Solomon king at Gihon Spring.
I was burning incense in the sanctuary of the Lord when the Archangel Gabriel appeared on the right side of the altar promising me a son.
I was the governor of Judah from David’s line who laid the foundation stone of the Second Temple alongside Joshua the high priest.
Struck down by heavenly light on the road to Damascus, I became the Apostle to the Gentiles and penned fourteen epistles.
explanation.am: ወደ ደማስቆ ስጓዝ በሰማያዊ ብርሃን ወደቅሁ፤ የአሕዛብ ሐዋርያ ሆንሁ፤ አሥራ አራት መልእክታትንም ጻፍሁ።

explanation.en: Called from casting nets in Galilee, I confessed Christ as the Son of the living God and preached at Pentecost.
explanation.am: ከገሊላ ዓሣ አጥማጅነት ተጠራሁ፤ “አንተ ክርስቶስ የሕያው እግዚአብሔር ልጅ ነህ” አልሁ፤ በበዓለ ኀምሳ ሦስት ሺህ አሳመንሁ።

explanation.en: I clave to Naomi saying “Thy God shall be my God”, gleaned in the fields of Bethlehem, and became ancestor to King David.
explanation.am: ኑኃሚንን “አምላክሽ አምላኬ ይሆናል” ብዬ ተከተልኋት፤ በቦዔዝ እርሻ ቃረምሁ፤ የንጉሥ ዳዊትም ቅድመ አያት ሆንሁ።

explanation.en: Dedicated to God by Hannah at Shiloh, I answered God’s midnight call and later anointed Saul and David as kings.
explanation.am: እናቴ ሐና በሴሎ ለእግዚአብሔር ሰጠችኝ፤ በሌሊት “እነሆኝ ተናገር” ብዬ መለስሁ፤ ሳኦልንና ዳዊትን በንጉሥነት ቀባሁ።

explanation.en: I was the wife of Abraham who received strength to conceive Isaac in my old age according to God’s faithful promise.
explanation.am: የአብርሃም ሚስት ነኝ፤ በእርጅናዬ ወራት በእግዚአብሔር ታማኝ ተስፋ ይስሐቅን በፀነሰ ጊዜ በደስታ ሳቅሁ።

explanation.en: I prayed for wisdom rather than riches, ruled over Israel at its golden peak, and built the holy Temple in Jerusalem.
explanation.am: ከሀብትና ከክብር ይልቅ ጥበብን ለመንሁ፤ እስራኤልን በሰላም መራሁ፤ በኢየሩሳሌምም የመጀመሪያውን ቤተ መቅደስ ሠራሁ።

explanation.en: Chosen as first of seven deacons, I saw the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God.
explanation.am: ከሰባቱ ዲያቆናት የመጀመሪያው ሆንሁ፤ ሰማያት ተከፍተው የሰው ልጅ በእግዚአብሔር ቀኝ ቆሞ አየሁ፤ በድንጋይ ተወግሬ ሰማዕት ሆንሁ።
